instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the lower middle, low enough to fit your Dutch oven with its lid on.

Cut 4 slices of the bacon into 1/4 inch strips. If your stew meat is in big chunks, cut it into 1 inch pieces. Peel the 3 carrots and cut them into 1/2 inch pieces, dice the onion and mince the 3 garlic cloves. Thickly slice the 8 oz mushrooms and halve the 1 lb potatoes.

Put the bacon in a large oven-safe Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook it for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's golden and the fat has melted out. Lift it out with a slotted spoon into a large bowl and leave the fat in the pot.

While the bacon cooks, pat the beef dry with paper towels and put it in another bowl. Sprinkle over 1 tsp of the salt and 3/4 tsp of the pepper, then the 3 tbsp flour, and toss until every piece is coated.

Turn the heat up to medium high. Add half the beef in one layer and leave it alone for about 3 minutes, until the underside is deep brown and lets go of the pan. Turn the pieces and brown the other sides for 3 to 4 minutes more, then move them to the bowl with the bacon.
Add 1 tbsp of the olive oil and brown the rest of the beef the same way. Move it to the bowl too.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, the carrots and the onion. Cook for about 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion starts to soften.
Add the garlic and the 1 tbsp tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until the paste turns a shade darker.

Pour in the 1 1/2 cups wine and scrape up all the browned bits from the bottom. Add the mushrooms and let it simmer for about 10 minutes, until the mushrooms are soft and the wine has cooked down a little.

Stir in the 3 cups broth, the 2 bay leaves, the 1/2 tsp thyme, the remaining 3/4 tsp salt and the last 1/4 tsp pepper. Put the beef, the bacon and any juices from the bowl back in the pot. Add the potatoes and push them down under the liquid. Bring it to a simmer.

Put the lid on and move the pot to the oven. Cook for 1 hour 45 minutes, until the beef breaks apart easily with a fork and the potatoes are tender. If the beef is still chewy, give it another 15 minutes.
Take out the bay leaves. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Serve in bowls with the crusty bread. If you're making it ahead, let it cool, cover it and keep it in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat it covered over medium low, stirring now and then, until it's bubbling.
method_notes: All three brown floured or seasoned chuck in batches, build the sauce on onion, garlic and tomato paste with red wine and beef broth, and cook it low and slow with carrots and small potatoes. Natasha's Kitchen starts with bacon, browns the beef in its fat, simmers sliced mushrooms in the wine and braises everything in a 325°F oven for 1 hour 45 minutes. RecipeTin Eats adds celery and Worcestershire and simmers it on the stove, lid on and then lid off, and Once Upon a Chef braises for 3 hours with balsamic and a little sugar and adds the vegetables for the last hour; it also says the stew tastes better made a day ahead. This follows Natasha's Kitchen, written for 4 and cooked in one pot instead of sautéing the vegetables in a second skillet.
